sources.entry: Geo2tz - Get the timezone from geo coordinates (lat, lon). MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Geo2Tz is a self-hostable HTTP service (and MCP server) that returns the IANA timezone for a given latitude/longitude pair using an offline timezone boundary database.
summary.what_it_does: Exposes a GET endpoint at /tz/{lat}/{lon} that returns the coordinates and matching IANA timezone name as JSON, and returns a 4xx response on invalid input. A second endpoint reports the version of the timezone database in use. Lookups run locally against a bundled timezone GeoJSON database, so coordinates are not sent to third-party services. Configuration is via GEO2TZ_* environment variables or an optional YAML, TOML, or JSON config file, including an optional token-based authorization check. The same binary can run as an MCP server over stdio, offering get_timezone and get_tz_version tools. The database can be updated with the geo2tz update command to a current, latest, or specific version.
use_cases: timezone lookup for an MCP-enabled AI assistant
determine local time zone for GPS points in an app
run a timezone microservice in Kubernetes or Docker
notable: Offline lookups: coordinates never leave the host, aimed at privacy-sensitive location data
Ships as an MCP server (stdio) with get_timezone and get_tz_version tools for AI clients
Docker image built FROM scratch containing only the binary and timezone database
Optional token authorization via query parameter
Built-in update command to fetch specific or latest timezone database versions
caveats: Local binary does not bundle the timezone database; it must be fetched with geo2tz update first
Docker image has no shell or curl/wget, so Compose healthchecks based on those will not work
Timezone data is sourced from timezone-boundary-builder, so accuracy depends on that upstream dataset
